FCNR(B) stands for Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) deposits. These are term deposits maintained by Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) in foreign currencies (like USD, GBP) with Indian banks.

faq.q: Why did the RBI close the special FCNR(B) swap window early?
faq.a: The RBI introduced this special facility to attract foreign currency inflows and strengthen India's balance of payments. It reportedly achieved its objective faster than expected, attracting nearly $57 billion in inflows, prompting the early closure.

faq.q: How do rising crude oil prices affect the Rupee?
faq.a: India imports a large portion of its crude oil. When global crude oil prices rise, India needs to spend more US Dollars to buy the same amount of oil, increasing demand for dollars and putting downward pressure on the Rupee.

faq.q: Does a weaker Rupee help anyone?
faq.a: Yes, a weaker Rupee benefits Indian exporters. When they sell their goods or services abroad and get paid in US Dollars, they receive more Rupees when they convert those dollars back to INR, boosting their earnings.
